title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§4 'Site de De Rham', previous page): for X/S, the site DR(X/S) has objects (U,U',i,π). Here U ⊂ X is open, i: U → U' is a nilpotent S-immersion, and π is a divided-power structure on J = ker(O_{U'} → O_U). Up to the absence of p-nilpotence and the nilpotence conditions, this is what Berthelot later called the crystalline site Cris(X/S). The subsite DR_strat ('De Rham strict/restreint') consists of the objects that locally on U' admit a retraction U' → U; the retraction is not part of the data. The undecorated sites are named analogously. Strat(X) is the stratifying site (nilpotent thickenings with local retraction, no PD). Cris(X), in this manuscript's naming, appears to be the infinitesimal site (nilpotent thickenings, no PD), i.e. Inf(X/S) of Grothendieck's 1966 'Crystals' lectures.

This page draws the commutative square of topoi
  Zar~(X) --> DR_strat~(X) -> Strat~(X)
                  |               |
               DR~(X)    ->    Cris~(X)
The vertical maps come from the inclusions of restricted sites; the horizontal maps come from forgetting divided powers. It makes four claims.
(1) If X is formally smooth over S, the vertical arrows are equivalences of topoi. For U' affine, formal smoothness lets one lift id_U to a retraction U' → U. So every object is locally in the restricted subsite, and the comparison lemma applies.
(2) If X is of characteristic 0 (e.g. S over Q), the horizontal arrows are equivalences. In a Q-algebra every ideal, in particular every nilpotent one, carries the unique PD structure γ_n(x) = x^n/n!. Forgetting the PD structure is therefore an isomorphism of sites.
(3) In DR(X) and DR_str(X), fibre products of two objects over a third, and kernels of pairs, exist. Over (V,V'), take U = U1∩U2 and U1' ×_{V'} U2'. The ideal is generated by the images of J1 and J2, and the PD structures glue on the tensor product over the PD base. He doubts the same holds for Cris(X) and Strat(X), marked with a '?'.
(4) Working in DR_strat(X): the sheaf X~ represented by (X,X) covers the final object. This is by definition, since a local retraction U' → U ⊂ X is a local section of X~. Hence there is a Čech (Cartan–Leray) spectral sequence
  E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X~^{ν+1}, O)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_{DR_str}, O).
The next page shows that X~^{ν+1} is ind-represented by the PD neighbourhoods Δ^{(ν)}(i)(j) of the diagonal in X^{ν+1}. The cohomology is thus computed by the cosimplicial system of PD-completed formal neighbourhoods of the diagonals. This is the 'Čech–Alexander' computation, which in the smooth case yields the de Rham complex. It is the route to the crystalline/de Rham comparison: Grothendieck's Crystals lectures for Inf, Berthelot for Cris, and later Bhatt–de Jong's Čech–Alexander complexes.
errors: The doubt about fibre products in the PD-less sites Cris(X) (infinitesimal) and Strat(X) seems over-cautious for the infinitesimal one. The same construction works there: U1∩U2 inside U1' ×_{V'} U2', with ideal generated by the two nilpotent ideals, hence nilpotent. For Strat (and DR_str), the real question is whether local retractability survives the fibre product; this is not addressed.

Products over the final object (e.g. X~ × X~) are not representable in DR_str. They are only ind-representable via PD envelopes, which are not nilpotent; the next page uses exactly this. This is consistent with claim (3), which is only about fibre products over a third object, but the site itself is not closed under the limits that the Čech computation needs.

The characteristic-0 statement needs only that O_S be a Q-algebra. 'X de car. 0' should be read as 'X over Q'. Also, the 'tranquilles' (tame) PD condition, whatever it is, must be compatible with the unique PD structure in characteristic 0.

missed.claim: A PD analogue of the stratifying site (DR_strat) is set up so that, even for non-smooth X, its cohomology is computed by the cosimplicial PD-formal neighbourhoods of the diagonals of X^{ν+1} themselves, with no smooth embedding needed. This is a minor, natural variant implicit in Berthelot's PD-stratification formalism. It is not usually singled out as a topos in its own right.
missed.quote: Travaillons dans DR_strat(X). Notons que l'objet X~ de DR_str associé à X couvre l'objet final
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it parallels the role of stratifying cohomology versus infinitesimal cohomology for singular X. It is a small historical detail on how crystalline cohomology was designed.

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational set-up of the crystalline site ('site de De Rham'): comparison of topoi and the Čech spectral sequence via PD neighbourhoods of the diagonal. All of it is close to Grothendieck's 1966 Crystals lectures and Berthelot's thesis. It is an interesting snapshot of the naming (Cris = infinitesimal, DR = PD site) and of the PD-stratifying variant, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out line at the top is illegible scribble ending in an arrow; it is fine as marked deleted.

'l'objet X~ de DR_str associé à X couvre l'objet final' is a good reading; the line actually runs 'l'objet X~ de DR_str couvre : X comme l'objet final (par définition des objets de DR_strat)', with 'associé' plausible.
'Si X est de car. 0' — the X is overwritten/struck and possibly corrected; the parenthesis reads '(par ex. S de car. 0)'.
'pour ces Cris(X) et Strat(X)' is more likely 'pour les' or 'pour des'.
'suite spectrale de Leray' — 'Leray' is an interlinear insertion above 'de'.
